cards.title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
cards.problemStatement:
You are given an array points representing integer coordinates of some points on a 2D-plane, where points[i] = [xi, yi].

The cost of connecting two points [xi, yi] and [xj, yj] is the manhattan distance between them: |xi - xj| + |yi - yj|, where |val| denotes the absolute value of val.

Return the minimum cost to make all points connected. All points are connected if there is exactly one simple path between any two points.

examples.explanation: We can connect the points as shown to get the minimum cost of 20. Notice that there is a unique path between every pair of points.
Connect all points to get the minimum cost.

solutions.solutionDescription: Use Prim's algorithm without a heap by maintaining a distance array. Start from any node, repeatedly find the unvisited node with minimum distance to the MST, add it, and update distances to remaining nodes. More efficient for dense graphs.
solutions.timeComplexityExplanation: We perform n iterations, and in each iteration we scan all n nodes to find the minimum distance node.
solutions.spaceComplexityExplanation: We use arrays of size n for distance and visited tracking.

solutions.solutionDescription: Build a Minimum Spanning Tree using Prim's algorithm with a min heap. Start from any node, repeatedly extract the minimum cost edge connecting an unvisited node to the MST. Add all edges from newly added node to heap.
solutions.timeComplexityExplanation: We process each of O(n^2) edges and each heap operation takes O(log n) time.
solutions.spaceComplexityExplanation: We store an adjacency list with O(n^2) edges and use a heap that can grow to O(n^2) size.

solutions.solutionDescription: Build MST using Kruskal's algorithm with Union-Find. Generate all edges with their costs, sort by cost, and process edges in order. Use DSU to check if adding an edge creates a cycle. Stop when n-1 edges are added.
solutions.timeComplexityExplanation: Generating all O(n^2) edges takes O(n^2) time, sorting them takes O(n^2 log n) time, and union-find operations are nearly O(1) amortized.
solutions.spaceComplexityExplanation: We store all O(n^2) edges in the edges array.
